title: Polymer Dye Synthesis Lab
description: A chemistry lab bench holds a coffee mug repurposed as a mixing beaker and a shoe mounted on a test stand as the dyeing target. The user must combine reagents in the mug following a specific reaction sequence, monitor temperature and pH conservation laws, apply the synthesized polymer dye to the shoe's material variants, and use undo/redo to correct mistakes across the multi-step process.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Scene setup: a lab bench plane with grid texture, warm overhead SpotLight, ambient HemisphereLight, and a PerspectiveCamera at (0,1.5,2.5) looking at origin. Load coffeeMug.glb on the left as a mixing vessel and MaterialsVariantsShoe.glb on the right on a small pedestal as the dyeing target. Implement a reagent panel UI (HTML overlay) with 5 colored reagent buttons (acid-red, base-blue, catalyst-yellow, solvent-clear, polymer-green). Clicking a reagent adds it to the mug: animate a colored sphere dropping in, change the liquid fill level inside the mug using a cylinder mesh whose height and color blend incrementally. Enforce conservation laws: total volume cannot exceed mug capacity (show a mL gauge, max 250mL, each reagent adds 50mL). Track pH as a numeric value (0-14) displayed on a floating label; acid lowers pH by 2, base raises by 2, others are neutral. Temperature gauge (20-100C) rises with catalyst (+15C) and acid (+10C), cools with solvent (-10C). The reaction succeeds only when pH is between 5-7 AND temperature is 60-80C AND polymer reagent was added last. On success, the mug liquid turns the final dye color with an emissive glow animation. The user then clicks an Apply Dye button which triggers a color-wash animation on the shoe, lerping its material color to the dye color over 1.5 seconds. Cycle through the shoe's material variants using a Variant dropdown so the user must dye at least 2 variants. Implement full undo/redo with Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y that reverts each reagent addition, restoring volume, pH, temperature, and liquid color to previous state using a history stack. Show step counter (target: 10-14 steps). Add a Reset Lab button that clears everything with a pour-out animation on the mug. All interactions should have subtle particle effects and sound-like visual feedback pulses.
